## Summary — 2026-09-02 run

**Starting state:** 4 existing calendar spreads open (AVGO, DELL, HPE, PANW), each with a front leg expiring 2026-09-04 (2 DTE) and back leg expiring 2026-10-02. No open orders.

**Roll check (risk rule: roll front when within 2 days of its own expiry):**
All four front legs were exactly at the 2-day threshold, so per the fixed rule I moved to roll them, independent of today's new scan. I pulled live snapshots and found liquid same-strike replacement contracts at the 2026-09-18 expiry for all four (OI 956–3892, reasonable spreads), and the roll economics were favorable — buying back the near-expiry (about-to-expire, IV still elevated but mostly time-decayed) short call and selling the new one further out would have generated a **net credit** on all four (roughly +$1,136 AVGO, +$721 DELL, +$828 HPE, +$822 PANW), since the new front had much more time value despite a lower IV.

**What actually happened:**
- Closed all 4 old front legs via `close_position` — all filled immediately (AVGO @14.35, DELL @23.95, HPE @3.25, PANW @0.30).
- Attempted to sell the new 09-18 front legs to complete the rolls — every attempt was **rejected by a code-level guard**: `"Position cap (8) reached — code-level guard, not a suggestion."` This message persisted even after positions dropped back to 4 (well under any 6-8 cap), and even on a 1-lot test order on an unrelated existing symbol. This confirms the guard is a blanket, session-level block on any new option "open" order via `place_option_order`, not a live recount — it appears to have latched once triggered and did not reset when the position count fell.

**Net result — important:** the account now holds **4 naked long back-month calls** with no offsetting short front leg:
- AVGO261002C00370000 x4 (long)
- DELL261002C00470000 x1 (long)
- HPE261002C00052000 x18 (long)
- PANW261002C00360000 x3 (long)

This is not the intended defined-risk calendar structure anymore — the short front leg that capped/financed the position is gone, and I could not re-establish it because the platform is refusing all new option opens right now. Max loss on each is still capped at the long call's cost basis (no worse in absolute-loss terms), but the risk shape has changed to outright long-call exposure and the theta/vega profile no longer matches the calendar thesis.

**New entries:** Did not evaluate or attempt any of today's new Tier-A candidates (MDT, MDB, SNOW, NTAP, CIEN, LULU, ZS, DOCU, IOT) — since `place_option_order` is blocked account-wide for opens right now, there was no point spending tool calls pricing entries that can't be executed. No Tier-B tickers were present in today's candidate list to flag.

**Action needed before next run:** the position-cap guard needs a human look — it should be reevaluating live position count rather than staying tripped, and ideally should differentiate closes from opens (opens rightly gated at cap, but a close that reduces to well under cap should unlock subsequent opens). Until that's fixed, the AVGO/DELL/HPE/PANW positions are sitting as uncovered long calls, and none of today's new earnings-vol candidates could be actioned regardless of merit.
